motion: Do cosmology, fine-tuning, origin-of-life research, biblical claims, and suffering make the Christian God more or less plausible?

lockedRoutes.description: Christian theism is supported cumulatively by a finite cosmic past, fine-tuning, the difficulty of naturalistic abiogenesis, biblical insight, and a redemptive account of suffering.
lockedRoutes.successCriteria: Show that several substantially independent considerations are more expected under a creator and Christian revelation than under scientific naturalism, while answering the principal scientific and moral objections.

motionBridge.description: The cumulative evidence makes the Christian God more plausible than scientific naturalism does.

centralBridges.description: A finite cosmic past is better explained by a transcendent creator than by matter alone.
Fine-tuning and life's information-rich origin materially favor intelligent design.
Biblical cosmological insight and its theological purpose support Christian revelation.
Suffering is compatible with a redemptive order governed by an eternal-good standard.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Several convergent arguments can support the conclusion without any single absolute proof.
Noncoercive evidence preserves freedom to accept or reject God.

lockedRoutes.description: Scientific skepticism argues that cosmology and fine-tuning underdetermine God, abiogenesis remains open, Genesis reflects ancient error, and suffering is improbable under Christian benevolence.
lockedRoutes.successCriteria: Defeat the claimed evidential bridges by exposing unsupported probabilities, viable alternatives, source or textual problems, and unresolved conflict between extensive suffering and a good Christian God.

motionBridge.description: The cited science, biblical claims, and suffering make the Christian God no more plausible and in important respects less plausible.

centralBridges.description: Current cosmology does not establish an absolute beginning or a divine cause.
Fine-tuning does not privilege God over brute fact, necessity, multiverse, or selection accounts.
Genesis contains ancient cosmological features better explained by human authorship.
Prehuman animal suffering and attributed divine violence conflict with Christian benevolence.

subsidiaryBridges.description: An unresolved natural origin of life is not positive evidence of divine design.
Explanatory probabilities require justified distributions and consistent evidential standards.

lockedSections.title: Cosmic beginning and infinity
lockedSections.rationale: The existence of an absolute beginning is a principal claimed scientific implication of theism and receives a direct, technically developed exchange.

proMoves.speaker: Michel-Yves Bollore
proMoves.proposition: The BGV theorem prevents an infinite regress of earlier expanding universes and therefore establishes some absolute cosmic beginning.

sourceSpan.excerpt: They have demonstrated that even if the big bang that we know is not the real beginning... this series is limited and therefore there has been an absolute beginning someday.

conMoves.speaker: Phil Halper
conMoves.proposition: Big-bang and BGV results do not establish that the universe began, because singularity results rely on disputed classical assumptions and BGV bounds inflation rather than the whole cosmos.

sourceSpan.excerpt: The big bang should be understood merely as a theory that says the universe evolved from a hot dense state... The theorem proves that inflation must have a beginning. The universe as a whole, it doesn't.

lockedSections.title: Fine-tuning and competing explanations
lockedSections.rationale: Fine-tuning is a major positive argument, and the debate directly compares design with multiverse, necessity, brute fact, and selection alternatives.

proMoves.speaker: Michel-Yves Bollore
proMoves.proposition: Life-permitting constants are extraordinarily sensitive, have moved scientists toward belief, and are more naturally explained by design because the multiverse lacks direct observation.

sourceSpan.excerpt: If we change just slightly one of these numbers then the universe does not exist... there are billions of other universe and we are lucky... the weakness of that is that nobody has seen anything of multiverse.

conMoves.speaker: Phil Halper
conMoves.proposition: Fine-tuning does not privilege God because inflation motivates a multiverse with predictive precedent, while brute fact, necessity, and selection remain live alternatives and no probability distribution has been justified.

sourceSpan.excerpt: It looks better than God... it's implied by inflationary cosmology... Weinberg predicted the value of the cosmological constant using the multiverse... What prediction has God made for anything observable in cosmology?

lockedSections.title: Origin of life and probabilistic inference
lockedSections.rationale: Abiogenesis is a distinct subsidiary evidential route, contested through the status of current research, expert relevance, and missing probability distributions.

proMoves.speaker: Michel-Yves Bollore
proMoves.proposition: The informational complexity of even a simple cell and the lack of a settled natural pathway make life's origin extraordinarily improbable without fine-tuned design.

sourceSpan.excerpt: Today there is no more idea of how life appeared from inert matter because the density of information... in the DNA of a cell is billion times billion time more dense than in a computer... it's completely improbable.

conMoves.speaker: Phil Halper
conMoves.proposition: The abiogenesis inference fails because the cited authority did not research life's origin, active hypotheses exist, and no probability distribution was supplied for declaring a natural origin improbable.

sourceSpan.excerpt: Where do you get the probability distribution... George, he didn't work on origins of life research... many labs around the world [are] working on origins of life. The leading hypothesis... is the RNA world hypothesis.

lockedSections.title: Genesis and scientific credibility
lockedSections.rationale: Biblical cosmology bears specifically on the Christian identification of God and generates a sustained exchange over alleged insight, ancient parallels, and genre accommodation.

proMoves.speaker: Michel-Yves Bollore
proMoves.proposition: Genesis was scientifically exceptional because the Hebrews rejected celestial divinities and described the sun and moon as created lights despite lacking advanced scientific institutions.

sourceSpan.excerpt: Everybody thought that the sun and the moon were divinity... the only tiny people... thought correctly that the sun and the moon were not divinity but they were just lamp in the sky.

conMoves.speaker: Phil Halper
conMoves.proposition: Genesis is not scientifically exceptional because its solid firmament reflects widespread ancient cosmology, and selective praise of apparent agreements while excusing errors as non-scientific is inconsistent.

sourceSpan.excerpt: There's nothing special... the sky is a solid dome known as the firmament... the Jewish encyclopedia [and] Hebrew English lexicon... regarded by the Hebrews as solid.

lockedSections.title: Animal suffering and divine moral authority
lockedSections.rationale: Prehuman suffering and biblical violence form the principal negative argument against Christian benevolence, with distinct pro defenses based on redemption and divine authority.

proMoves.speaker: Michel-Yves Bollore
proMoves.proposition: Earthly suffering belongs to a post-fall redemptive world in which opportunities for good action enable humanity to return to paradise.

sourceSpan.excerpt: God has sent men to another world... which is what we need today to go back to God... We need to do good deeds and we can do good deeds only in the world where there is unfortunately evil.

proMoves.speaker: Michel-Yves Bollore
proMoves.proposition: Human and animal death is not immoral for God because God can restore life, and eternal separation from God is the only ultimate evil by which divine actions should be judged.

sourceSpan.excerpt: There is only one thing which is bad for God... losing men... for eternity... the only goal of God is to bring as many men back to paradise.

conMoves.speaker: Phil Halper
conMoves.proposition: Hundreds of millions of years of prehuman animal suffering and biblical commands or actions harming animals are substantially more expected if the Christian God does not exist than if that God is benevolent.

sourceSpan.excerpt: Animals have been suffering for hundreds of millions of years before humans existed... Why would a good God choose such brutal processes... God ordered the genocide of the Amalekites. He included the animals.

conMoves.speaker: Phil Halper
conMoves.proposition: A theology that cannot condemn genocide and gratuitous animal killing loses its moral standard, because divine power to restore life does not justify choosing cruel means.

sourceSpan.excerpt: If you can't say because of your religion that a genocide is evil, then you can't say anything isn't evil. You've lost your moral compass... If that isn't evil, what the hell is?
